lesson_title: Three Tricks That Make a Drawing Look Real
hook_text: Flat pencil lines become a solid steel crank with three tricks. No talent required.
clip_script: Here is how designers make a drawing look real enough to pick up. Trick one, colour. A different colour for each part, and let the colour hint at the material: brown for wood, grey for metal, bright for plastic. Trick two, shading. Pick where the light comes from, top left, and stick to it. Surfaces facing the light stay pale, surfaces facing away go dark, round things fade from one to the other, and a shadow underneath stops it floating. Trick three, texture. Wavy lines for wood grain, a sharp white stripe beside a black one for shiny steel. Now apply it: a disc on a shaft becomes a cam you can almost touch, an arm on an axle becomes a crank. No measurements anywhere, those live on the working drawing. This is an artist's impression, and it is how an idea gets sold before it is built.
visual_style: A flat outline of a crank gains flat colour, then graded shading with a sun icon top left, then a metallic highlight stripe; the final render rotates slightly beside the original outline.
pacing: Three tricks of fifteen seconds each, then a ten-second reveal of the finished crank and cam.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and render one cylinder from flat to shiny in four steps.
